title: Scalp Massage: How to Do It and Does It Help Hair Growth? — cv.cm
description: How to do a scalp massage with fingertips or a silicone brush, a 4-minute routine, oil or not, and what the small studies on scalp massage for hair growth found.
h1: How do you do a scalp massage, and does it help hair grow?
answer: Place the pads of your fingers on the scalp and move the skin in small, slow circles without sliding over the hair, working from the hairline to the crown and down to the base of the skull. Four minutes is enough. It may help you relax. One small 2016 study in nine men found slightly thicker hair, but scalp massage is not a hair-loss treatment.

body: The key is to move the scalp, not the hair. Press the pads of your fingers, not the nails, into the scalp until the skin moves over the skull. Then make small circles about the size of a coin. Lift the fingers, move 2 to 3 cm, and repeat.

ul: Light pressure: the fingers slide over the hair. This does little for the scalp.
Medium pressure: the scalp skin moves with your fingers over the bone. This is the target, about 4 to 5 on a 1 to 10 scale.
Firm pressure: you feel the bone strongly. It should still feel comfortable. Sharp or burning pain means stop.

body: Keep your nails short or keep them off the scalp entirely. Scratching can break the skin and irritate hair follicles. Rubbing back and forth fast can tangle and break long hair, so slow circles work better.

sections.h: Dry, in the shower, with oil, or with a brush

head: Method
How to do it
Good to know
rows: Dry, with fingers
Sit upright or lie down. Do the routine through dry hair.
Easiest to do at a desk or in bed. No product needed.
In the shower
Massage while you shampoo, using the shampoo as a slip.
Use lukewarm water, not hot. Rinse well so no shampoo stays on the scalp.
With oil
Part the hair and apply a few drops of a plain oil to the scalp, then massage. Wash it out after.
Oil is optional. It can make dandruff or oily scalps worse and can cause irritation. Test a small spot first.
With a silicone scalp brush
Hold the brush flat and make small circles, the same as with fingers. Let the soft nubs move the skin.
Use the same medium pressure as fingers. Do not scrub. Rinse and dry the brush after each use.

body: Oil massage of the head has a long history in South Asian, Southeast Asian and other traditions. There is no evidence that any particular oil makes the massage itself work better. Choose by comfort and how your scalp reacts.
The same routine works dry or in the shower. Use a timer if you want to keep to the times, for example cv.cm's countdown set to 4 minutes.

head: Step
Area
What to do
Time
rows: Front hairline
Both hands, fingers spread, small circles from the center of the forehead hairline out to the temples.
Sides above the ears
Fingers above and behind the ears, circles moving up toward the crown.
Top of the head
Circles along the center line from front to back, ending on `GV20`.
Crown and back
Both hands at the back of the head, circles moving down toward the base of the skull.
Base of the skull
Thumbs under the skull ridge on both sides, steady pressure on `GB20`.
Finish
Spread the fingers, grip a handful of hair close to the roots, and pull very gently for 2 seconds. Repeat over the head.

body.note: The 2016 hair study used 4 minutes a day. That is a useful reference length, not a proven dose.

body: Two acupressure points are easy landmarks for this routine. Locations follow the WHO Standard Acupuncture Point Locations in the Western Pacific Region (2008). One cun is about the width of your thumb at the knuckle, and four fingers held together are about 3 cun. Qi and meridians are traditional ideas. Here the points simply mark useful spots.

head: Point
Standard location
How to find it
How to press
rows: Baihui (`GV20`), Hundred Meetings
On the head, 5 cun above the front hairline, on the midline
Fold the tops of both ears forward. Draw an imaginary line over the head from the top of one ear to the other. Where it crosses the midline, you will often feel a slight hollow.
Middle finger or both middle fingers stacked. Press straight down, pressure 3 to 5, 30 to 60 seconds, or small circles.
Fengchi (`GB20`), Wind Pool
Below the base of the skull, in the hollow between the upper ends of the sternocleidomastoid and trapezius muscles
Slide the thumbs up the back of the neck to the base of the skull, then slide each thumb outward about two thumb-widths until it drops into the hollow between the two large neck muscles.
Both thumbs, pressing up toward the skull, never toward the throat. Pressure 4 to 6, 30 to 60 seconds, 2 to 3 rounds.

sections.h: What the research says about hair growth
body: The study most often quoted is by Koyama and colleagues, published in the journal Eplasty in 2016. Nine healthy Japanese men without obvious hair loss used a scalp massage device for 4 minutes a day on one side of the head for 24 weeks. Hair thickness in the massaged area increased slightly. However, the paper also reports no significant difference in thickness between the massaged area and the untreated area, the hair count fell at 12 weeks, and hair growth rate did not change. The study was small, had no women, and was partly funded by a company with a commercial interest.

That is very limited evidence. It does not show that scalp massage regrows hair, prevents hair loss, or helps people with hair-loss conditions such as pattern hair loss or alopecia areata. Scalp massage is not a hair-loss treatment.

If you are losing hair, see a doctor or a dermatologist. The NHS advises seeing a GP if you are worried about hair loss, and before you pay for a commercial hair clinic. Some causes, such as thyroid problems, low iron, certain medicines or scalp infections, need a medical check. A doctor can also explain treatments that have been tested.

Many people find scalp massage relaxing. A Korean study of 34 female office workers (Kim and colleagues, 2016) gave scalp massages of 15 or 25 minutes twice a week for 10 weeks and reported favorable changes in stress hormones (cortisol and norepinephrine) and blood pressure compared with a control group. The study was small, so treat this as a hint, not proof.

The NHS lists relaxing activities, including massage, as something that may help tension-type headaches. A gentle scalp and neck massage can be part of that, together with breaks, sleep and fluids. It is not a migraine treatment, and it does not replace medicine your doctor has advised.

sections.h: Safety, mistakes and when to see a doctor

ul: Scratching with nails: use the finger pads only. If you leave red lines or flakes of skin, you are pressing with the nails.
Rubbing too fast: slow circles move the scalp. Fast rubbing tangles and breaks hair.
Hair pulling: keep the pull very gentle. Tight pulling or tight hairstyles can damage hair over time.
Too much oil: a few drops are enough. Wash it out the same day if you get dandruff or spots.
Sore scalp the next day: halve the pressure and time.

body: Skip the massage over cuts, scabs, a rash, a scalp infection, an active flare of psoriasis or eczema, or a recent head injury. People taking blood thinners or with a bleeding disorder should use light pressure only. After a hair transplant or any scalp surgery, ask the surgeon when massage is safe.

body.note: Get emergency care for a sudden, extremely painful headache, a headache after a head injury, a headache with a stiff neck and fever, or a headache with confusion, weakness, numbness, loss of vision or trouble speaking. See a doctor soon for a sore, tender scalp with jaw pain when eating, sudden patchy hair loss, or hair loss with an itchy, scaly or painful scalp.

faq.q: How long does scalp massage take to grow hair?
faq.a: There is no reliable timeline because there is no good evidence that scalp massage grows hair. The only well-known study lasted 24 weeks in nine men and found a slight change in thickness. See a doctor or dermatologist for hair loss.

faq.q: Is it OK to massage your scalp every day?
faq.a: Yes, a few minutes a day with the finger pads at medium pressure is fine for most adults. Stop if the scalp becomes sore, red or itchy.

faq.q: Is a silicone scalp massager better than fingers?
faq.a: Neither has been shown to be better. A soft silicone brush can be easier in the shower and keeps nails off the scalp. Use the same small circles and gentle pressure.

faq.q: Does oiling the scalp help hair growth?
faq.a: There is no good evidence that oiling the scalp grows hair. Oil can make massage more comfortable, but it can also worsen dandruff or irritate the skin in some people.

faq.q: Can scalp massage help a headache?
faq.a: Many people find gentle scalp and neck massage relaxing during a tension-type headache, and the NHS lists massage among relaxing activities that may help. A sudden or severe headache needs medical care instead.
